- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply decay to subsequent days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.53) and model forecasts are below recent highs, increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 10-day average is >10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (0.00–0.27) and price is trending downward, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag; add 1–3% upward adjustment to catch reversal early.
